correctness.rationale: Use the bipartition {x,v_i} and {y,u_i}. Incident edges are automatically compatible; disjoint edges are compatible exactly when neither of their two crossed edges is present. This gives internal compatibility of each of the three page families. The spine forbids every middle edge, the spine is a witness against every left–right pair, and a side edge can occur with a middle edge only on the same page (a different middle edge has its corresponding side edge as a witness). Thus with the spine the contribution is z[2(1+z)^m−1]. Without it, the three single-family subsets contribute 3(1+z)^m−2 and the only additional sets are the 2m same-page middle/side pairs. For m≥2 all terms except the spine contribution have degree at most m, giving exactly its two full-star maxima. At m=1 the polynomial is 1+4z+4z² and the same-page pairs furnish the other two maxima.
residual_risks: The supplied exhaustive output is recorded evidence, not a fresh run. Its replay path is verify.py for m=1,…,6, covering 599184 subsets; the compatibility proof is independent of those finite results.

value.rationale: The shared-edge square-page book is a standard cyclic family; its allowable individual injective-color classes do not factor independently across pages. The theorem resolves every size coefficient and shows exactly how the spine enforces the two optimizing stars, while middle transversals and the exceptional same-page pairs survive without it. This gives a reusable full profile and optimizer description rather than just a small evaluation or a scalar family bound.
residual_risks: No analogous polynomial for longer-page books, or number of complete injective colorings, is established.
